summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V1.3.2 as MODIFIED from 4.0.3 V5.2.4 and covering V5.5.4. V5.2.4 required avoiding eval() or other dynamic code execution, and sanitizing or sandboxing user input where there was no alternative. V5.5.4 required JSON.parse in browsers or JavaScript backends and forbade eval() to parse JSON.

Issue #309 in this snapshot is “2.1.4 Attestation information,” an authentication item; Andrew van der Stock’s 18 November 2018 “Resolve #309” is tagged V5.2.4 in git but is not this eval clause. Mapping and the two predecessors are the origin.

The 5.0 text keeps the eval() ban, names Spring Expression Language (SpEL) as an example of dynamic execution, and requires sanitizing included user input where there is no alternative. It drops V5.2.4’s sandbox option and does not carry forward V5.5.4’s explicit JSON.parse sentence even though mapping says that control is covered.

kisasondi’s 26 February 2019 validation-chapter update and Andrew van der Stock’s 1 March 2019 “Update to final text” are tagged V5.5.4 and are the JSON.parse predecessor’s 4.0 freeze, not a documented SpEL insertion. Authentication and V12 commits on this slot are unrelated.
